page: Microsoft Azure E128-32ads_v7 is an Eadsv7-family virtual machine running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V45 processor with x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The configuration includes 32 vCPUs, derived from 16 physical cores with 2 threads per core. Memory capacity is 1024.0 GB, yielding a high resource density of 32.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is bundled with a capacity of 7559 GB, and there are no complimentary public IPv4 addresses. No GPUs are present on this instance.

Benchmark data reveals distinct performance characteristics. Single-core CPU performance is in the top tier according to stress-ng, and single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression also reach top-tier levels. Multi-core performance is more moderate, with stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and PassMark physics tests falling into the average category. Memory bandwidth tests for both small and large blocks consistently register in the average range, though the overall PassMark memory score is strong.

Tradeoffs are evident in workload-specific benchmarks. While small-model LLM inference achieves top-tier text generation speeds, scaling to a large 70B parameter model results in poor performance for text generation. Database operations and Redis SET operations perform at average levels. Given the high memory-to-vCPU ratio and substantial local storage, this server is configured for memory-intensive workloads, large databases, and single-thread-heavy processing tasks, rather than massive multi-threaded compute or large-scale LLM inference.
